events.subtitle: NOW'S THE TIME — 75th Anniversary
events.category: Living Japanese jazz master / 75th-anniversary strings program / alto-led orchestral jazz
events.factual_description: Sadao Watanabe's official site lists Sadao Watanabe with Strings 'NOW'S THE TIME' at Meguro Persimmon Hall on Tuesday, December 1, 2026. Doors are at 18:00 and the performance starts at 18:30. Reserved seats are ¥10,000 for S and ¥9,000 for A. The verified rhythm section is Russell Ferrante on piano, Ben Williams on bass and Ittetsu Takemura on drums, with Takayuki Oshikane Strings: a 20-player ensemble of twelve violins, four violas and four cellos. Tokyo Onkyo bills the concert as part of Watanabe's 75th anniversary. General ticket sales are scheduled to begin September 26, 2026 at 10:00; the earlier Ticket Pia advance lottery closed August 30. The same with-strings production is also scheduled in Utsunomiya on November 28 and at Suntory Hall on December 3, so no one-off, farewell or final-performance claim is inferred.

en.why_it_matters: The anniversary becomes a present-tense musical proposition rather than a retrospective because Watanabe puts the alto in front of a twenty-player string body while Russell Ferrante, Ben Williams and Ittetsu Takemura keep a compact rhythm section underneath it. That scale changes the room around one of Japan's foundational living jazz voices: orchestral color is added without removing the instrumental directness and pulse that make the saxophone the center of the music.
en.trip_verdict: If December 1 overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for Meguro and let the 18:30 concert anchor the evening. The December 3 Suntory realization of the same production gives a Tokyo stay some scheduling flexibility, so I would choose the date that fits the trip rather than contort a wider Kanto itinerary around only one of the two halls.
